classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish neither, exactly one and at least one failure using the regions of two overlapping sets.

content.prompt:
Solve the problem by drawing a Venn diagram.

In a factory, 1000 light bulbs were subjected to two quality control tests $A$ and $B$. Five hundred and sixty passed test $A$ and 410 passed test $B$, while 150 passed both tests. How many light bulbs:

answer.worked:
Let $A$ and $B$ be the sets of bulbs passing tests $A$ and $B$, respectively. The Venn diagram has 150 in the overlap.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number passing A only}&=560-150\\\text{Number passing A only}&=410\\\text{Number passing B only}&=410-150\\\text{Number passing B only}&=260\\\text{Number failing both}&=1000-410-150-260\\\text{Number failing both}&=180\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number passing A only}&=560-150\\\text{Number passing A only}&=410\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number passing B only}&=410-150\\\text{Number passing B only}&=260\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: passed only one of the tests?

answer.worked:
Add the two non-overlapping regions inside the circles.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number passing exactly one}&=410+260\\\text{Number passing exactly one}&=670\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: failed at least one of the tests?

answer.worked:
Every bulb except those passing both tests failed at least one test.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number failing at least one}&=1000-150\\\text{Number failing at least one}&=850\end{align*}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: failed in only one of the tests?

answer.worked:
Failing exactly one test means passing the other test, so use the two regions outside the overlap but inside the circles.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number failing exactly one}&=410+260\\\text{Number failing exactly one}&=670\end{align*}$$

spec.mathematics: A only 410; intersection 150; B only 260; neither 180; universal total 1000.
